# Base image with OpenMPI, Flux, and AWS EFA support for ARM
FROM ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm

# Set non-interactive frontend for package installations
ENV DEBIAN_FRONTEND=noninteractive

# Install build dependencies, including build-essential, cmake, git, and certificates
# We clean up the apt cache in the same layer to reduce image size
RUN apt-get update && \
    apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends \
    build-essential \
    cmake \
    git \
    ca-certificates && \
    apt-get clean && \
    rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*

# Set a working directory for the application examples
WORKDIR /opt/lammps-reax

# Clone, build, and install LAMMPS in a single layer to optimize image size
# - Clone the latest version of the LAMMPS source code.
# - Create a build directory.
# - Configure the build with CMake, specifying MPI compilers and enabling the REAXFF package.
# - Compile the source code using all available processor cores.
# - Copy the main LAMMPS executable to a system path.
# - Copy the required example files into the WORKDIR.
# - Clean up the cloned source code to minimize the final image size.
RUN set -e && \
    cd /tmp && \
    git clone --depth 1 https://github.com/lammps/lammps.git lammps-src && \
    cd lammps-src && \
    mkdir build && \
    cd build && \
    cmake \
      -D CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release \
      -D BUILD_MPI=yes \
      -D CMAKE_CXX_COMPILER=mpicxx \
      -D CMAKE_C_COMPILER=mpicc \
      -D PKG_REAXFF=yes \
      ../cmake && \
    make -j$(nproc) && \
    cp lmp /usr/local/bin/ && \
    cp /tmp/lammps-src/examples/reaxff/HNS/* /opt/lammps-reax/ && \
    rm -rf /tmp/lammps-src

# Verify that the lmp executable is in the system's PATH
RUN which lmp

#
# MiniCluster manifest to run a LAMMPS ReaxFF experiment on a single AWS ARM-based node.
# This configuration is for testing purposes and uses the Flux Operator to manage the job.
#
apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  # A descriptive name for the LAMMPS experiment MiniCluster
  name: lammps-reax-hns-aws-arm
  # As per instructions, deploy to the default Kubernetes namespace
  namespace: default
spec:
  # The number of pods to create for the MiniCluster.
  # For this test, we are running on a single node.
  size: 1

  # The total number of MPI tasks for the job.
  # The LAMMPS command with "-v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2" implies a 2x2x2=8 processor decomposition.
  tasks: 8

  # Maximum number of nodes the cluster can expand to.
  # This fulfills the requirement to be able to run on up to 4 nodes.
  maxSize: 4

  # Keep pods and resources after the job finishes for inspection and debugging.
  cleanup: false

  # Enable strict logging to catch potential configuration issues.
  logging:
    strict: true

  # Flux-specific configurations for the job execution environment.
  flux:
    # Disable the separate Flux sidecar container. Flux will be started within the main application container.
    container:
      disable: true
      # Since this is an ARM instance, a specific ARM-compatible Flux image is required.
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
    # Explicitly set the architecture to ARM.
    arch: "arm"

  # Define the list of containers for the MiniCluster Pods. Only one is needed.
  containers:
    # The application container image for the LAMMPS experiment.
    - image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax

      # The command to be executed by the Flux scheduler across the specified tasks.
      # Flux automatically prepends 'flux run -n <tasks> ...' to this command.
      command: lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite

      # This container runs the main workload and is not a job launcher.
      launcher: false

      # Always pull the container image to ensure the latest version is used for experiments.
      imagePullPolicy: Always

      # Resource requests and limits for AWS-specific hardware.
      # This requests an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) for low-latency, high-bandwidth internode communication.
      resources:
        limits:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
        requests:
          vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1

apiVersion: flux-framework.org/v1alpha2
kind: MiniCluster
metadata:
  name: lammps-reax-hns-aws-arm
  namespace: default
spec:
  cleanup: false
  containers:
  - command: lmp -v x 8 -v y 8 -v z 4 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite
    image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/fractale-agent-experiments:lammps-reax
    imagePullPolicy: Always
    launcher: false
    resources:
      limits:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
      requests:
        vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
  flux:
    arch: arm
    container:
      disable: true
      image: ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy
  logging:
    strict: true
  maxSize: 4
  pod:
    nodeSelector:
      node.kubernetes.io/instance-type: m7g.16xlarge
  size: 4
  tasks: 256

manager.name: Build and Deploy LAMMPS
manager.description: Build a Docker container and deploy it as a Kubernetes Job.

context.environment: AWS CPU instance in Kubernetes to run across nodes
context.details:
You MUST use ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-openmpi:ubuntu2204-efa-arm as a base image. It includes OpenMPI and libfabric provided from the efa installer for AWS and the entire Flux Framework stack.
You MUST compile lammps setting the cxx compiler to mpicxx and the c compiler to mpicc.
Ensure all globbed files from examples/reaxff/HNS from the root of the lammps codebase are in the WORKDIR. Clone the latest branch of LAMMPS. You MUST put lmp on the PATH and run which lmp to ensure success.
You MUST build LAMMPS for a multi-node MPI environment

context.optimize:
You MUST maximize the LAMMPS FOM, *atom steps per second.  It could be Matom or katom.
You MUST choose the largest problem size to maximize FOM. You MAY go up to 4 nodes. 
You MUST make an effort to increase problem size as much as you can.
context.resources: The resource spec you got earlier is for an autoscaling cluster, so the nodes possible are not there. You must add the nodeSelector to use node.kubernetes.io/instance-type m7g.16xlarge with 64 CPU, 256 GiB Memory, ARM (Graviton3). You are limited to up to 4 nodes.
context.testing: Run in.reaxff.hns in the pwd with lmp -v x 2 -v y 2 -v z 2 -in ./in.reaxff.hns -nocite for testing only on all processes of one node.
context.details:
You MUST run on up to 4 nodes and you MUST set flux.container.disable to true.
You MUST set the containers imagePullPolicy to Always.
The Flux Operator uses flux run in the pwd with the tasks determined by the spec.tasks.
You MUST set resource requests and limits to use vpc.amazonaws.com/efa: 1
Since this is an ARM instance you MUST change the flux.container.image to be
ghcr.io/converged-computing/flux-view-ubuntu:arm-jammy and set flux.arch: "arm".
